validator_result: OK. These warnings were expected. Four lines say the planned patterns rally-allies and resupply-allies are not filled in yet. The shared WARN line lists tempest-rising.veti.shepherd among the unit links to units not researched yet. Two ATYPICAL lines appear, and both are recorded in the unit's atypical list under their exact rule strings with notes: 'weapon-families:blades allowed.damage-types kinetic' (armament/0/family) and 'weapon-families:explosives allowed.weapon-delivery projectile' (armament/1/family). format-json rewrote nothing, and --check reports the file formatted.

hesitations.reason: The rule is clear but the result fits badly. The designation 'Reanimated Sacrificial Thrall' names no role (registry note). Step 2 reads the main button only for unarmed or tool-only units, and the fists do damage. So the unit goes to step 5 as a medium-speed generalist, and its real job (being spent on Sacrifice) is never read. Recorded in fit_notes.

hesitations.chosen: support, buffer (both at step 1, in roles-list order)
hesitations.reason: Two readings are open. First, the 2.0.0 Veti notes move Enlightened into the game's 'Support' category instead of army units, for the All Army hotkey. Does a selection category count as official text calling the unit by the role label? Second, the 27 May 2026 beta build guide calls them a 'Buff unit'. Is 'buff' a word form of 'Buffer / aura', and does this pre-2.0.0 text still count under 'use the newest official text'? Support's requires pass only through the resupply-allies link.
The unit is never bought. The band allows null only in games with no purchases, and the validator errors on null for tempest-rising. Very-low is used as the nearest band, with a fit_note.
raw is 'the base price paid', and none exists. 0 would band as very-low too, but it would claim a price.
Both buildings spawn it. The Anchor route needs no tech, and the infobox says tier 1.
The rule is clear: the figure equals the Field Scout's. The source is unclear: the wiki prose calls Enlightened 'weak and slow', and the figure comes from a page verified at the second beta.
Damage step 4 binds: the infobox gives the Rifle type, and the damage_map sends it to kinetic. The blades family lists only melee, electric and energy.
The infobox reach (300) is far under 0.7 of the reference (2500), so the figure alone gives short. Melee's coding rule (blows land at touching distance) was preferred for fists.
The Ground targets line and no label lead to step 4. Subjugating Attack works only on infantry, but the punches themselves can be ordered at any ground target.
Neither passes the same-interaction test for Subjugation. The registry note says to leave patterns empty and add a fit_note.

The Phantom Caster comes from the Refined Enlightenment doctrine, bought mid-match. The slot rules name only bought upgrades, research and ranks, and doctrines are closest to research. There is no button, so it is not alternate.

The sources say the grenades are hurled: the Seeker Codex, and the wiki's 'grenade-like projectiles'. Under the delivery rule a thrown object counts as a shot seen travelling. No source describes an arc, which lobbed would need, and the explosives family lists no projectile delivery.

The makers' Seeker line says it hurls the grenades at infantry and structures. I read that as a step-3 label naming the targets. Read as 'good-at' wording instead, it would send the weapon to step 4, and the Ground line would add vehicles.

Paired entries links upgrade-in-field only for an upgrade bought on the unit or for all units at a building, when it reaches units already in the field. A doctrine is bought from the side's menu, and no page says whether fielded Enlightened switch weapons.

Per the registry note, the extra perks are the receivers' own and are recorded on them. Self-destruct fails because Sacrifice does no damage. Using up the giver is covered by no pattern, so I added a fit_note.
The automatic sacrifice on death comes only with the Sacrificial Symbiosis doctrine. The stock ability is a targeted button.

hesitations.chosen: Subjugating Attack in the weapon summaries, not as an ability
hesitations.reason: The registry note says a wN_passive goes in the weapon's summary and is never an ability.
The blast and the Servitors come from other units' buttons or perks, and the automatic sacrifice from a doctrine. None of them is the unit's own outcome, so they go in notes.
The validator requires a non-empty list because the fists do harm, but no source names anything the unit beats. role:anti-armour would cover tanks, which crush it.
The Sniper damage category maps to kinetic, which would also cover rifles, so I used weapon:sniper. Crushing is limited to medium and heavy vehicles, and both map to heavy.

unclear_rules.topic: Never-bought units in a game with costs
unclear_rules.note: cost_band.band allows null only when units are not bought in the game. A unit that is never bought gets no honest band; I used very-low with no raw.
Unclear whether the 2.0.0 notes' selection category 'Support' (instead of 'army unit') counts as official text calling the unit by the support label at roles.secondary step 1.
Unclear whether 'Buff unit' names Buffer / aura. The word list's examples (harasses for harasser) suggest yes.
Unclear whether the pre-2.0.0 beta build guide still counts when a newer post speaks to the unit without contradicting it.
Only unarmed or tool-only units are read by their main button. A sacrificial support unit with weak fists lands in assault at step 5.

Paired entries names only upgrades bought on the unit or at a building. Doctrines are bought from a side menu, and the rule is silent on them, even though doctrine abilities take source commander-power.
Lobbed needs an arc described, the explosives family bans projectile, and its default delivery (place) is wrong for a thrown grenade.
Unclear whether an official line saying what a weapon is thrown 'at' (infantry and structures) is a label or good-at wording.
The validator demands a non-empty counters list for any unit with a harming weapon, even when no source names anything it beats. Only reasoned entries were possible.

unclear_rules.topic: Effects that depend on the receiver
unclear_rules.note: The registry note puts Consecrated perks on the receivers, while the giver's Sacrifice links only the generic patterns. How far the giver's entry should carry the receivers' effects is not written down.
The Status effect page lists Prone as a positive effect, so Subjugated infantry may be unable to go prone. No rule needs this, but it touches the prone note.

new_mechanics.summary: The weapon's hits mark enemy soldiers: while marked they cannot receive any positive effect (auras, buffs), and any that die marked rise as weak units for the attacker's side. Counterplay: kill or outrange the markers, keep infantry back or send vehicles, which are immune, and do not count on buffs for marked troops.

The same Subjugating Attack, carried on the doctrine-granted Phantom Caster grenades: hit infantry cannot be buffed and rise as Enlightened if they die marked. Counterplay as for armament/0, and splash makes clumped infantry the easy prey.

source_problems: The Enlightened page is verified only at 1.8.0+57892, the second Veti beta, and still carries a pre-release Upcoming banner. Its health, speed, sight and weapon figures are from the beta, and the 2.0.0 Veti post names no change to them. The Resources page gives old spawn intervals (70 and 50 seconds). The Resurrection Anchor and Corral pages and the 2.0.0 post give 55 and 47 (recorded as sources_disagree). The pages disagree on Consecrated Reaping. The Enlightened and Status effect pages say structures make 20 resources every 5 seconds. The Ability page says 10 credits every 5 seconds and lists no units, while the Anchor Accrual doctrine gives Caretakers 20 credits every 2 seconds. On prone, the Unit page lists the Enlightened among standard infantry who go prone, but the Status effect page names only six other soldiers (recorded as sources_disagree). The Phantom Caster has no page of its own; its data is on the Enlightened and Seeker infoboxes. The Corral infobox still shows pre-2.0.0 cost and health. The Status effect and Caretaker pages carry no Verified tag. Correction made during coding: an early search of the Veti Arsenal page made me credit the Cultivator with 'each sacrificed Enlightened spawns a Combat Servitor'. The makers' specialists post (701027957162902189) and the Ziggurat sidebox both give that line to the Ascended, so I fixed the Sacrifice summary and the uncertain notes before the final checks. The registry note's 'older Cultivator line' on the Veti Arsenal is real: its Cultivator row is shorter than the tooltip. All pages came from the local cache, and no network fetch was needed this session.
